Hi Voat,

This request might be a little different from what you're used to, or rather, this may be a very normal request from an unlikely source. I'm the executive director of a hip-hop arts nonprofit in the US and we're currently developing plans for a listening club. In short, we're going to be bringing people together at bars, after-school programs, and other social settings to listen to albums from the history of hip-hop from start to finish. The goal, in part, is to give people a space to celebrate these cultural achievements and provide them with a shared experience (listening to the album) from which they can discuss other issues in life. I'll gladly answer any questions to give you all a better grasp of the program, but my need is to come up with a series of seven albums over seven weeks to use for our pilot run of the program. There aren't many rigid requirements for what we'll use: no bar on lyrical content, no required level of market success, no particular era we're looking for. But we'd like to find albums that mattered in one way or another and would like to find some way to make them feel like a real series, not just seven albums slapped together into a nice package. Ideally, we'd like to feature seven different artists/groups as well, but we could be flexible here. Also, diversity is a cornerstone, so while doing a run of all early 90's East Coast albums would be great, we're looking to spread a wider base with this first series. Later on, we'll likely do specific, targeted mini-runs of similar albums.

Thanks for your time and your collective thoughts, ~ Mike

I was having horrendous GPU performance after upgrading to Windows 10. So, I read doing a system refresh was a good way to fix poor performance. I backed up my HDD to an external drive and then ran a system refresh (rather than full reset). Everything seemed fine until it attempted to boot. My system is stuck in a boot loop cycle. It powers on, shows the blue Windows logo, a spinning ball thing shows up, then it blue screens with the error "INACCESIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE". I've tried booting from my backup in BIOS and that didn't work either. Its possible for me to boot using my Windows 7 install disk but I'm not sure if I'll lose all of my data if I do so. I could really use some help.

That message usually either means a driver for your hard drive or SATA ports is missing, or more commonly the file system is corrupted.

My usual fix is to put the hard drive on a USB adapter to fix it from a healthy computer, but you can probably boot from a recovery disk and get to a command prompt to run chkdsk c: /f

It's a bit tricky because when your computer is in the state it's in at the moment, there is no way to boot from the hard drive to fix it.

Pretty rare to see that error these days so might be worth running speedfan to check your hard drive SMART status.

Only other thing I can think of is to make sure your external drive is disconnected, and that the bios hasn't been changed to IDE / compatibility more.

Windows can't boot from a USB external drive. You would need to restore that backup or physically swap the drives if it was a clone backup.

In rare cases, having a cloned drive connected can cause weird stuff to happen if windows decides it lives partly on the clone rather than the original drive.

If you have a backup of all your files, the best way to go is probably a clean install. You did the update first, so your license should work automatically if you do (it worked fine on my fresh install). You'd need to download the Media Creation Tool on another PC to create installation media. You can download this tool >here<. Run the tool and choose to create installation media for another pc, rather than update. This way you can create either a DVD or a USB boot drive to do a fresh install on your own PC. Set the BIOS to run from either your USB or DVD, boot into the Windows install and Bob's your uncle. When you're asked for your license key, just click "later" or "not now". It will activate automatically after the installation.

This is assuming you copied all your files from your harddrive to an external one rather than creating a system image.
